question.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined by 

$$
A=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-x\ge {y}^{2}\}.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\text{int}\,A\cup ∂A=A$

II. $A⊂\text{int}A$

III. $A-\text{int}A=∂A$
question.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

In this case, the set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14134863/assets/88f35519cf1aa01bcc9e4fb91b24c2bc2a1a823867ec2670563b0b45f2643a0a.png)

The interior of a set $A,$ denoted $\text{int}\,A,$ is the set containing all the interior points of $A.$ It contains every point in $A$ except the boundary points: 

$$
\text{int}\,A=A-∂A
$$

The interior of $A$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14134863/assets/649c33f1738a35f3d298038bd2cf05d3b435424a4efbbb1e6143cf0d56b2bfd6.png)

 

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement I is true. Since $\text{int}\,A$ contains all points in $A$ except the boundary points, we must have $\text{int}\,A\cup ∂A=A.$

- Statement II is false. In this case, the set $A$ contains all of its boundary points, so we must have $A⊈\text{int}A.$

- Statement III is true. Since $\text{int}\,A$ contains all points in $A$ except the boundary points, we must have $A-\text{int}A=∂A.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
